correction: There is no Companies Act 2019 in the Bahamas; the governing statute is the Companies Act, Chapter 308 (Act No. 18 of 1992, as amended through 2025).
There is no Companies Act 2016 in Barbados; the governing statute is the Companies Act, Cap. 308 (originally 1982, as amended through 2020).
There is no Companies Act 2016 in Antigua and Barbuda; the governing statute is the Companies Act, 1995 (Act No. 18 of 1995, as amended through 2024).
There is no Companies Act 2012 in Grenada; the governing statute is the Companies Act, Cap. 58A (Act No. 35 of 1994, as amended through 2022).
The Companies Act in St. Lucia is Chapter 13.01 (1996), not Cap. 8.01; Chapter 8.01 is the Companies and Intellectual Property (Registry) Act.
The governing statute in Dominica is the Companies Act, Act No. 10 of 1995 (CIPO), which the row cites only generically with no year; the IBC regime (not companies) was discontinued in 2022.
Asociaciones civiles in Guatemala are governed by the Código Civil, not the Código de Comercio, as the row states; REPEJU registration with the Ministerio de Gobernación is correct.

The 1983 associations law (Decreto-Ley 1346) is correct, but the fideicomiso is governed by Ley 741 (2010), not 'Ley 395/1998' (Ley 395 is an unrelated 2001 interpretive law), and there is no standalone 'Ley de Fundaciones' — foundations fall under Decreto-Ley 1346/1983 and Ley 147/1992.
Ley 218 is the Ley de Asociaciones of 8 August 1939, not 1920.
The fideicomiso is governed by Ley 1 de 1984 (Por la cual se regula el Fideicomiso en Panamá), not 'Ley 10/1994'; Ley 25/1995 on fundaciones de interés privado is correct.
Fundaciones are governed by the Civil Code (arts. 88-97) with Cámara de Comercio registration, not Ley 793 de 2002, which is a derogated extinción de dominio law.
The Ley Orgánica de Fundaciones dates from 1961 (with 1985 amendments), not 2001.

Asociaciones and fundaciones are both governed by the Civil Code (arts. 109-119, 200-211); Ley 27258/2000 only created a district in Huánuco and Ley 27907 is a tax treaty with Canada, so both law numbers are misattributed.
Ley 351/2013 (Otorgación de Personalidades Jurídicas) is real, but the co-operative law is Ley 356/2013 (Ley General de Cooperativas), not 'Ley 2440'.

Co-operatives are governed by the Co-operative Societies Act Cap. 88:01 (1948, as amended), not a 'Co-operative Societies Act 1984'; Companies Act cap. 89:01 and Friendly Societies Act cap. 36:04 are correct.
Ley 1984 is the 1929 Ley de Sociedades Cooperativas, not '1999'; Ley 5833/2017 (OSC) and Ley 6446/2019 (registry) are correct.
Asociaciones civiles and fundaciones are governed by Ley 17.163 de 1999, not Ley 17.296, which is the 2001 national budget law.
Ley 27.290/2016 is the fideicomisos (trusts) law, not a foundations law; foundations are governed by Ley 23.851 and CCyC arts. 193-224.
Mongolia has no '2013 NGO law'; the governing statute is the Law on Associations (1997), alongside the Civil Code (2002) and the 2015 Law on State Registration of Legal Entities.

Law 16/2021 is Macau's immigration (entry/exit control and residence) law, not a foundations law — private foundations are governed by the Civil Code (arts. 1642-1667) and no new foundations/associations law was in force at verification (the associations regime law was still in public consultation in 2026, replacing Civil Code provisions and Law 2/99/M).
Law name is correct, but the Incorporated Societies Act 2022 came into force on 5 October 2023; 6 April 2026 is the date the old 1908 Act ceased to apply and reregistration became compulsory.
Companies Ordinance 1979 was repealed and replaced by the Companies Act 2021 (in force from 2021), so it is no longer the current governing law for companies.
The Business Corporations Act is 1990 (P.L. 1990-91, 52 MIRC Part I), not 1981; the Trust Act of 1994 is correct.
The Foundations Law is No. 5736 (20 Feb 2008), not 5737; the current associations law is No. 5253 (2004), which replaced the 1984 Law No. 2860.

The civil-association law cited as 'Lei 9/10' is wrong — Lei n.º 9/10 of 30 June 2010 only abolished the Assembleia Nacional's Constitutional Commission; the governing private-associations law is Lei n.º 14/91 of 11 May 1991 (Lei das Associações Privadas).

No Luxembourg '1912 law' on associations exists - ASBLs are governed by the loi du 21 avril 1928 sur les associations et les fondations sans but lucratif (now abrogated/replaced by the loi du 7 aout 2023), and foundations fall under the same 1928/2023 laws, not a '2003 law'.

Since 2015 private foundations (Privatstiftungen) are governed by the federal Bundes-Privatstiftungsgesetz (BGBl. I 15/2015), not state-level Stiftungslandesgesetze, and the charitable tax status of a nonprofit GmbH rests on KStG para 7 (donations: EStG para 18), not 'EStG para 7'.

There is no 'PGR 2013 Stiftungsgesetz' and the article numbers are wrong: foundations are PGR (20 Jan 1926) Art. 552-570 (revised 2002), Vereine are PGR Art. 246 ff., and the Anstalt is PGR Art. 534-551 - not Art. 1031 ff. or Art. 55 ff.

Andorra has no 'Law 14/2003' on foundations - fundacions are governed by the Llei 11/2008 de fundacions (since 2023 the consolidated Llei 17/2023), and associations by the Llei qualificada d'associacions of 29 December 2000.

Associations (zdruzenia) are governed by Act 83/1990 Coll. o zdruzeni obcanov, not 'Act 85/1985', and VPO public-benefit status is granted under Act 213/1997 Coll. (neziskove organizacie poskytujuce vseobecne prospejne sluzby), not 'Act 65/2018' (which amends the surveyors/appraisers law); the nadacia cite (Act 34/2002) is correct.
ok - NGO Law Sl. list CG 39/2011 (amended 37/2017, 84/2024) confirmed, with 3+ founders at Art. 10; note foundation establishment is also Art. 10, while Arts 25-27 govern foundation organs.

Neither named law is right: Law 1566/1985 is an education law (associations are governed by the Civil Code arts. 59/78), and no foundations 'Law 40/2022' exists; foundations fall under Civil Code arts. 144-162 and the new public-benefit-foundation framework Law 5259/2025 (replacing Law 4182/2013).

There is no 'Non-Not-For-Profit Organisations Act' of 2021; voluntary organisations (associations, foundations, trusts) are governed by the Voluntary Organisations Act (Chapter 492), enacted 2007 and amended since.

Norway has no national associations act; the 2020-21 draft 'lov om foreninger' was never enacted, so member associations remain unregulated (selvstendig forening) and are simply registered at Brønnøysund.
There is no '2023 Foundation Act'; Danish foundations are governed by the Foundations Act (lov om fonde og visse foreninger, LB 938/2012) - Law no. 753/2023 is an unrelated social-law omnibus.

There is no 2016 NVO law; NVOs are registered in the Enterprise Register as associations/foundations under the Law on Associations and Foundations (Biedrību un nodibinājumu likums, 2014, in force 2015), the old 1995 NVO registration law having been repealed.
Israel's governing statute is the Associations Law 5740-1980; '5725-1965' is the Succession Law, so the cited number is wrong.

UAE has no Federal Decree-Law 11/2018 private-foundations act nor FDL 2/2019 associations act (11/2018 relates to civil service/antiquities, 2/2019 is the ICT Health Law); charitable associations are governed by Federal Law 2/2008 on Public Benefit Associations, as amended by Federal Decree-Law 50/2023, with foundation regimes only at emirate/free-zone level (DIFC, ADGM).
Law 19 of 2006 is Bahrain's Labour Market Regulation Act; NGO/civil organizations are governed by Law No. 21/1989 regulating social associations, clubs and private institutions.
Yemen's NGO framework is Law No. 1 of 2001 concerning associations, foundations and NGOs under the Ministry of Social Affairs and Labour, not a '73/1991' NGO law.
Palestinian societies register under Law No. 1 of 2000 on Charitable Societies, Social Bodies and Private Institutions; no '1996 Societies Law' exists (Law No. 1/1996 is the Condominium Law).
Egypt's civil-society regime is Law 70/2017 on associations and foundations (with Law 149/2019 introducing the notification regime); neither 'Law 84/2014' nor 'Law 149/2014' exists.
No "Law No. 51/AN/71 of 1971" exists (Djibouti's legislature began only after 1977 independence); associations are formed under the inherited French Law of 1901 on Associations.
There is no "NPO Act 2003" (and the Companies Act is 2001, not 2015); NPOs/associations register under the Registration of Associations Act 1978 (Act 35 of 1978).
Non-profit companies in Pakistan are incorporated under Section 42, not Section 21, of the Companies Act 2017.
There is no "NGO Regulatory Authority Act 2008"; the governing NGO law is the Foreign Donations (Voluntary Activities) Regulation Ordinance 1978, with registration through the NGO Affairs Bureau.
There is no "Public Trusts Act 1950" in Sri Lanka (that is an Indian/Bombay statute); charitable trusts are governed by the Trusts Ordinance (Cap. 72).
The NGO law is the NGO Act 2001, not an "NGO Trust Act 1997"; registration is handled by the Department of Employment & Workplace Safety (not a "Department of Social Services").
The main NGO law is the Law on Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs) of 2005, not an "NGO Law 2015" (the NGO Registration Committee is real).

No Maldivian 'Public Trusts Act' (2022) exists; charitable trusts are governed by the Income Tax Act (Law 25/2019) charitable-organization approval and general trust arrangements, while private companies fall under the Companies Act (Law 7/2023) — the named 'Companies Act 2023' matches only the year, not a 2023 statute number.
Décret n° 92-130/PMRT of 27 May 1992 on NGO-government cooperation was abrogated by décret n° 2022-002/PR of 5 January 2022 (art. 30), so it is outdated; the 1901 association law itself is correct.

Loi L/2005/014/AN of 4 July 2005 governs cooperatives and non-financial mutuals (groupements économiques à caractère coopératif), not NGOs; ONGs in Guinea are regulated under Loi L/2005/013/AN (associations) plus government approval decrees.
The governing law is Federal Law No. 7-FZ of 12 January 1996 'On Non-Commercial Organizations' — '99-FZ' is a typo (99-FZ of 2011 is the licensing law).
